answer: Each identity locks 90 credits at the bridge and claims one river crossing per epoch. A crossing counts when its crystal clearance matches the identity key, epoch, and river ledger hash; the auditor recomputes the ledger from public crossings and burns the bond on mismatch or reuse. The fee rises per identity: the k-th pays 20+4(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 4,016 and 1,000 fakes pay 2,018,000 plus 90,000 locked. A rented-bridge-pass ring fails: a rented crystal clearance names its original key, so reuse burns the bond. An honest agent pays 20 once and recovers 90 after a clean epoch.
